title: Coffee Shop Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. Eri Kisaki (Ran's mother, an attorney) is kept as a node -- she is one of the four suspects tested for the stall-gap fit and is central to the on-screen deduction, not a background cameo. Sonoko and the unrelated Wakaoji/Sonoko subplot are omitted as out of scope for the murder case itself. Correcting the v1 scaffold: the true mechanism is not "the killer climbs over, then wipes the wall clean" -- the killer never crossed the gap at all. He stabbed the victim outside the stall and threw her body over the gap to block the door from the inside, which is why blood is found above the door despite the killer being fully unbloodied and never having climbed anything; the stall-gap fit test (which only clears Sumeragi and Kisaki) is itself a red herring. The retrieval "rope" is Tonoyama's own ring-finger bandage, re-fastened after the murder to hide the victim's blood on it. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The restroom window, the supposed escape route for an outside mugger, is unnaturally clean -- given the amount of blood loss, a killer climbing out through it should have left traces, and a fleeing mugger who abandoned the murder weapon wouldn't have paused to wipe the glass. Rules out the outside-job theory.

Blood is found on top of the stall door that the body was blocking -- but the killer was never sprayed with blood at all. The blood got there because the victim's body, not the killer, went over the gap: she was stabbed outside the stall and thrown in afterward.

The knife's handle is bloody but a narrow band near the handle is completely clean, as if something had been tied tightly around exactly that spot -- consistent with a cord used to pull the blade back out of the stall after the body was dumped.

The same clean-strip-in-a-bloody-surface pattern from the knife handle also appears on the victim's handbag handle, corroborating that a cord was tied taut against multiple objects at the scene rather than the knife's pattern being incidental.

Tonoyama's bandage sits on exactly the finger a wedding ring would occupy, and the timeline shows it was re-fastened after he arrived at the coffee shop -- during the window when the murder took place -- rather than before, contradicting his claimed rugby-practice injury.

Yayoi asks the bartender where the restroom is even though she'd already been told, moments earlier, that it was unisex -- an odd question to ask twice unless it wasn't really a question, but a signal to someone waiting to know she was heading there.

A physical fit test through the narrow gap above the stall wall clears everyone except Sumeragi and Kisaki, who can just barely squeeze through -- seemingly ruling out the larger Tonoyama and Wakaoji entirely, since the prevailing theory assumed the killer had to climb the gap in person.
